Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
candidates.comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: broadcastAffiliateOf
candidates.comment: An organization representing the media network(s) whose content is broadcast on a broadcast service. Also called: network affiliation, broadcast network. Examples: "BroadcastService 'Local TV Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NBC'", "BroadcastService 'Radio Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NPR'."

relations.embedding_query_text: hosted:

candidates.label: hostingOrganization
candidates.comment: A hosting organization relation between a member program or program membership and the organization that offers or manages it. Also called program provider, membership organization, host company. Examples: "A member program has a hosting organization 'Airline X'.", "The program membership is with a hosting organization.", "This program is hosted by a specific organization."

candidates.label: gameServer
candidates.comment: A game server relation between a video game and the server where it can be played. Also called: hosted on, playable server, game host. Examples: "Minecraft" game server "Hypixel Network", "World of Warcraft" game server "Frostmourne Realm", "Call of Duty" game server "Dedicated Server". Distinct from game, which is the game itself.

candidates.label: isStoreOn
candidates.comment: A platform hosting relation between an online store and the e-commerce marketplace where it operates. Also called hosted on, operates on, platform for, marketplace for. Examples: An online store isStoreOn 'Amazon'. A small business's online store isStoreOn 'Etsy'. A vendor's shop isStoreOn 'eBay'.

candidates.label: game
candidates.comment: A game relation between a game server and the video game that is hosted and played on it. Also called: hosted game, server game, game played. Examples: "Minecraft Server" game "Minecraft", "World of Warcraft Realm" game "World of Warcraft", "CS:GO Server" game "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive".

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: homeTeam
candidates.comment: A home team relation between a sports event and the team or person designated as the home participant. Also called host team, home side, local team. Examples: "A sports event has a home team 'Lions'.", "The match features a home team.", "This event's home team is a specific person."

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: returnPolicyCountry
candidates.comment: The country designated as the destination for product returns under a merchant return policy. Also called return destination country, country for returns, return shipping country. Examples: `US Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"US"`, `European Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `Country: Germany`, `International Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"CA"`.

candidates.label: arrivalStation
candidates.comment: A station where a train trip concludes. Also called: train destination, end station, terminal station. Examples: "TrainTrip 456 arrivalStation 'Grand Central Station'", "TrainTrip from Rome arrivalStation 'Termini Station'", "TrainTrip to Berlin arrivalStation 'Hauptbahnhof'". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which specifies the specific platform within a station.

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: arrivalAirport
candidates.comment: An arrival airport relation between a flight and the airport where it concludes. Also called destination airport, landing airport, final airport. Examples: "A flight's arrival airport is 'LAX'.", "The flight's arrival airport is 'Heathrow Airport'."

candidates.label: deliveryAddress
candidates.comment: A destination relation between a parcel delivery and its destination postal address. Also called: shipping address, recipient address, delivery location. Examples: "Package" delivery address "123 Main St, Anytown, USA", "Food Order" delivery address "Apt 4B, 567 Oak Ave", "Mail" delivery address "P.O. Box 100".

candidates.label: arrivalBoatTerminal
candidates.comment: An arrival boat terminal relation between a boat trip and the terminal or port where it concludes. Also called destination boat terminal, disembarkation port. Examples: "A boat trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Port of Miami'.", "The ferry trip's arrival boat terminal is 'Dover Terminal'."

relations.embedding_query_text: was part of:

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: partOfTVSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a TV episode, season, or clip and the TV series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

candidates.label: program
candidates.comment: An association between a program membership and the specific member program it belongs to. Also called part of program, associated program, membership program. Examples: "A loyalty card membership is part of the 'Star Alliance Gold' program.", "A gym membership is part of the 'Premium Fitness' program.", "A frequent flyer membership is part of the 'SkyMiles' program.". Distinct from programName, which is the textual name of the program.
